column1: You are attracted to someone charismatic, but you notice they often use "sarcastic" humor to put others down. How should you evaluate this?
column2: Accept it as "iron sharpening iron" in a unique way. (Proverb 27:17)
column3: Recognize beauty is fleeting, but a person without discretion is like a gold ring in a pig's snout. (Proverb 11:22)
column4: Trust that their "charming" personality will eventually win over your family. (Proverb 31:30)
column5: View their success as proof that "the diligent will bear rule." (Proverb 12:24)

column1: You are tempted to be lazy and skip shifts at your job. What does Proverb say about the consequences of slothfulness?
column2: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, so you should focus on your mental health first. (Proverb 13:12)
column3: B. "Pride goes before destruction," so you should avoid working too hard. (Proverb 16:18)
column4: C. "A slothful hand makes poor," while the hand of the diligent makes rich. (Proverb 10:4)
column5: D. "The fear of the Lord makes one rich," so work ethic is irrelevant to wealth. (Proverb 10:22)

column1: You are browsing social media and see seductive images that cause you to struggle with lust in your heart. What does wisdom advise?
column2: Do not lust in your heart after her beauty, nor let her captivate you with her eyes. (Proverb 6:25)
column3: Follow your eyes, because "the light of the eyes rejoices the heart". (Proverb 15:30)
column4: Keep browsing, because "a merry heart does good like medicine". (Proverb 17:22)
column5: Trust that God will Provide a way of escape without you having to change your behavior. (Proverb 3:26)

column1: You start hanging out with a new group of popular kids, but they consistently make poor choices (cheating, gossiping, etc.). What does wisdom advise?
column2: Keep hanging out with them; a man who has friends "must himself be friendly." (Proverb 18:24)
column3: Walking with the wise makes one wise, but a "companion of fools will suffer harm". (Proverb 13:20)
column4: A good name is better than riches; their popularity makes them good connections. (Proverb 22:1)
column5: D. "The fear of the Lord makes one rich," so their lack of fear won't affect you. (Proverb 10:22)

column1: A new person joins your youth group leadership team, and they are younger and have less experience. How might a wise person approach this situation, considering the value of learning and guidance mentioned in Proverbs?
column2: Disregard their input because of their age and inexperience.
column3: See it as an opportunity to mentor and support them, recognizing that everyone starts somewhere and wisdom can be gained.
column4: Immediately give them the most difficult tasks to see if they can handle it.
column5: Assume they are naturally wise and don't need any guidance.

column1: You have a long assignment due, and you're tempted to procrastinate until the last minute. What does wisdom from Proverbs suggest about a timely work ethic?
column2: It's okay to delay; "hope deferred makes the heart sick," so waiting is natural. (Proverb 13:12)
column3: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can give a reason. (Proverb 26:16)
column4: He who hastens with his feet sins, so you should work slowly. (Proverb 19:2)
column5: slothful hand makes poor, while the hand of the diligent makes one rich. (Proverb 10:4)

column1: You are presented with an opportunity to join a business venture that promises incredibly quick, high returns but seems ethically questionable. What is the wise approach?

column3: Avoid it; wealth obtained by vanity or quickly gained will diminish. (Proverb 13:11)
column4: Pursue it, because "where no counsel is, the people fall". (Proverb 11:14)
column5: Trust that "the rich man's wealth is his strong city". (Proverb 10:15)

column1: You are making choices about your future. What does wisdom suggest is the fundamental difference in outcomes between a righteous path and a wicked path?

column3: The path of the wicked is simply more fun, leading to immediate happiness.
column4: Both paths lead to the same destination, so the choices don't matter much.
column5: The wicked are protected by "riches," making their path safer than the righteous. (Proverb 10:15)

column1: You’ve been single for a long time and feel pressured to date anyone who is available. How should you view the wait?

column4: Realize that "all the paths of the Lord are mercy," even if you settle. (Proverb 3:6)

column5: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished. (Proverb 13:11)

column1: A person you know commits adultery and ruins their marriage. What is the long-term result for the adulterer?
column2: They will be able to start over easily with a clean slate.
column3: They will get "wounds and dishonor," and their reproach will not be wiped away. (Proverb 6:33)
column4: Riches avail not in the day of wrath, so only financial loss is a problem. (Proverb 11:4)
column5: "The good man leaves an inheritance," so their legacy is secure. (Proverb 13:22)

column1: You have a close friend who has been there for you during a very difficult time. How does Proverbs describe this type of bond?
column2: A man that has friends must show himself friendly, it’s transactional. (Proverb 18:24)
column3: Iron sharpens iron, so the friendship is just about self-improvement. (Proverb 27:17)
column4: A friend loves "at all times," and a brother is born for adversity. (Proverb 17:17) (p. 38)
column5: In the multitude of counselors there is safety, it's just one piece of advice. (Proverb 11:14)

column1: Someone asks for a small amount of money that you can easily give. What does wisdom suggest?
column2: Say not, ‘Go, and come again,’ when you have it with you. (Proverb 3:28)
column3: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due. (Proverb 3:27)
column4: He that gives to the rich, shall surely come to want. (Proverb 22:16)
column5: "A man that has friends must show himself friendly," so give to friends only. (Proverb 18:24)

column1: You've had a long week of work and studying. How should you view your time for rest and leisure?
column2: Rest is for the weak; only constant work is godly.
column3: Rest is a necessary part of life that allows for refreshment and perspective, preventing burnout.
column4: Rest should be used to plan your next "get rich quick" scheme.
column5: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, so rest is an integrity issue (Proverb 11:3)

column1: A friend who is wealthy consistently acts arrogantly toward service staff. What does Proverbs say about the wealthy who act this way?
column2: They should be careful, because the "rich answers roughly, but the poor uses entreaties". (Proverb 18:23)
column3: Their actions are fine because "a rich man's gift enlarges him". (Proverb 18:16)
column4: Pride goes before destruction, especially if you are poor. (Proverb 16:18)
column5: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, so the rich are always guided. (Proverb 11:3)

column1: A friend often seeks out risky, dangerous activities for "fun" and laughs at your caution. What does wisdom say about their choices?
column2: They are brave, as "the righteous are bold as a lion". (Proverb 28:1)
column3: A man of understanding is of an excellent spirit, so they must understand the risk. (Proverb 17:27)
column4: They are following their heart, which is a good guide. (Proverb 4:23)
column5: They "despise wisdom" and court destruction with their lack of care. (Proverb 1:7, Proverb 10:23)

column1: You want to share your partner's flaws with your friends to get "advice." What is the danger?
column2: A man who has friends must himself be friendly. (Proverb 18:24)
column3: A talebearer reveals secrets, which separates close friends. (Proverb 11:13)
column4: In the multitude of counselors there is safety. (Proverb 11:14)
column5: He who covers a transgression seeks love. (Proverb 17:9)

column1: You've made a financial promise to a small business owner. Now you want to delay payment. What is the instruction?
column2: Say, "Go and come again, and tomorrow I will give," if you now have it. (Proverb 3:28)
column3: Do not withhold good from the owners thereof, when it is in your power to act. (Proverb 3:27)
column4: C. "The rich answer roughly," so it is better to delay the payment slightly. (Proverb 18:23 (p. 41))
column5: He who hastens with his feet sins, so you should take your time paying them back. (Proverb 19:2)

column1: The Bible compares involvement with an immoral person to a bird darting into a snare. What does this imagery imply?
column2: It will be a brief moment of excitement with no lasting effects.
column3: The person knows they are in danger but ignores it.
column4: They have no sense and little know it will cost them their life. (Proverb 7:23)
column5: In the multitude of counselors there is safety, so the bird just needs advice. (Proverb 11:14)

column1: Someone shares a secret with you and swears you to confidentiality. Later, another friend asks you about the matter. What should you do?
column2: Tell them, because "open rebuke is better than secret love". (Proverb 27:5)
column3: Keep silent, because "he who has a faithful heart conceals a matter". (Proverb 11:13)
column4: Tell them in general terms, because "in the multitude of words there cannot want iniquity." (Proverb 10:19)
column5: A fool utters all his mind, so you should just be honest with everyone. (Proverb 29:11)

column1: You see someone in your youth group being unfairly blamed for something. What does a wise approach to fairness suggest you should do?
column2: Speak up truthfully and respectfully about what you know to help ensure a just outcome.
column3: Stay out of it to avoid any trouble. (Contrast with standing up for justice)
column4: Spread rumors about the person doing the blaming to get back at them.
column5: Assume the person being blamed must have done something wrong anyway.

column1: When planning a leisure activity, what is a wise consideration to keep in mind?
column2: How expensive it is, because "the rich man's wealth is his strong city". (Proverb 10:15)
column3: A man of understanding is of an excellent spirit, so anything that makes you feel smart is good leisure. (Proverb 17:27)
column4: If all your friends are doing it, it must be fine. (Proverb 13:20)
column5: That you "ponder the path of your feet" and consider whether it is a wholesome and wise activity. (Proverb 4:26)

column1: You have limited income but feel led to be generous. What does the Bible suggest about the attitude of giving, regardless of wealth?
column2: You can't give if you are poor; only the rich can be generous.
column3: A "liberal person shall have plenty," as scattering generously often increases resources. (Proverbs 11:24-25)
column4: Only give so that you may "have a good name," which is better than riches. (Proverbs 22:1)
column5: He that is surety for a stranger shall be sore vexed, so avoid giving. (Proverbs 11:15)

column1: What is the final destination for the house built by "folly" or lack of wisdom?
column2: It seems right for a time, but its "end is the ways of death". (Proverb 14:12)
column3: It will be a strong city because the "rich man's wealth is his strong city". (Proverb 10:15)
column4: It will be an inheritance for their children's children. (Proverb 13:22)
column5: It will stand because "through wisdom a house is built". (Proverb 24:3)

column1: You are becoming emotionally obsessed with a new crush. How do you handle your focus?
column2: Trust in the Lord with all your heart and let your emotions run free. (Proverb 3:5)
column3: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it spring the issues of life. (Proverb 4:23)
column4: A merry heart does good like medicine, so enjoy the obsession. (Proverb 17:22)
column5: Commit your works to the Lord and your thoughts will be established. (Proverb 16:3)

column1: You start making a lot of money at a new job. How should you view wealth?
column2: Riches and honor are with me when you find wisdom. (Proverb 8:18)
column3: He who trusts in his riches will fall. (Proverb 11:28 )
column4: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children. (Proverb 13:22)
column5: Wealth makes you secure, as "the rich man's wealth is his strong city". (Proverb 10:15)
